title: Past and future polar amplification of climate change: climate model intercomparisons and ice-core constraints
problem: This paper addresses the significant spread among climate models in simulating polar amplification by comparing past and future scenarios and using paleoclimatic reconstructions from ice cores to constrain model results and reduce uncertainty.
method: The paper proposes a model-data comparison method to constrain polar amplification by correcting climate model outputs for ice-sheet elevation and seasonal precipitation biases before comparing them with paleoclimatic reconstructions from ice cores for past and future climate scenarios.
task: The task is to evaluate polar amplification of climate change in various climate models for past and future scenarios by comparing their simulations with each other and with paleoclimatic constraints from ice-core data.
